question: How much of the external local-PCA witness removal is explained by matched random 8D subspaces?
control: deterministic zero-mean orthonormal random 8D basis; same anchors, property, per-anchor local-PCA sigma scale, valid-pixel/mean/clip conventions, solver; seeds 0,1,2.

LARD.network: 1152-64-32-3 ReLU MLP (pitch tercile), external LARD V2
LARD.reading: Random 8D subspaces are UNSAT on all 150 queries at every alpha for both bounded and unbounded encodings. They remove every broad-ball witness removed by local PCA. The same-extent brightness band (R2) removes no witnesses, separating the LARD removal from pixel-ball extent. Valid-pixel constraints do not change the random-control result.

mnist_fc.network: VNN-COMP mnist_fc mnist-net_256x2 (not trained by us)
mnist_fc.local_pca_headline: bounded local PCA @1sigma UNSAT on all 50; removes 23/23 resolved broad witnesses
mnist_fc.reading: Random 8D subspaces with valid pixels are UNSAT on all 450 queries (50 anchors x 3 seeds x 3 alphas), including 69/69 broad-SAT-anchor queries at 1 sigma. They remove every resolved broad witness at every alpha, at least as completely as local PCA, which has one SAT at 2 sigma. The mnist_fc removal is explained by a bounded low-dimensional region.

unified_conclusion: Across TinyTaxiNet (P3), external LARD, and external mnist_fc, a matched random 8D subspace verifies or removes at least as well as local PCA. The local-PCA verification-rate and broad-witness-removal gains are explained by low-dimensional-region effects; local PCA still provides a data-aligned support model and recovers witnesses random subspaces miss in P3.
